purpose: Glatiramer is used to treat relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis (MS). It helps reduce the number of MS flare-ups (relapses) you experience. It does not cure MS, but it can help slow down how often your symptoms get worse.
how_it_works: MS happens when your immune system mistakenly attacks the protective coating around your nerve fibers. Glatiramer is made up of proteins that look similar to that protective coating, so it essentially 'distracts' your immune system away from attacking your nerves. Over time, this helps reduce inflammation and damage in your brain and spinal cord.
common_side_effects: Redness, pain, swelling, or a lump at the injection site are very common. You might also experience flushing, chest tightness, heart pounding, shortness of breath, or anxiety shortly after injecting — this usually passes within 15-30 minutes and is generally not dangerous. Other common effects include weakness, nausea, joint pain, and skin rashes.
warnings: Tell your doctor right away if you have severe chest pain, difficulty breathing, or feel like you might faint after injecting. Long-term injections in the same spot can cause a permanent dent or discoloration in the skin, so always rotate your injection sites. Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding before starting this medication.
typical_dosing: Glatiramer is given as an injection under the skin (subcutaneous). The typical dose is either 20 mg injected once daily, or 40 mg injected three times per week (at least 48 hours apart). Your doctor or nurse will teach you how to inject it safely at home. Always rotate where you inject to protect your skin.
